item.title: Expats Set to Tip Tightest Swedish Electoral Race in Century
item.description: The tightest Swedish vote in a century may come down to expat ballots.
item.dc:creator: Flavia Krause-Jackson

item.title: Thailand Election Commission Refers Senate-Rigging Cases to Court
item.description: Thailand’s Election Commission decided to refer dozens of cases of alleged Senate vote-rigging to the Supreme Court, a potential new challenge for Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul’s ruling Bhumjaithai Party.
item.dc:creator: Patpicha Tanakasempipat

item.title: Lula Edges Ahead of Bolsonaro Amid Court Crisis, New Poll Shows
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva edged ahead of Flávio Bolsonaro in a new poll ahead of October’s vote, as the latest twist in Brazil’s Supreme Court crisis renewed scrutiny of the right-wing challenger’s ties to a disgraced executive at the center of a multibillion-dollar banking fraud.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Rosati

item.title: Iran-Gulf Talks Delayed as Saudi Arabia Counters Houthi Attacks
item.description: A meeting between Iran and several Gulf Arab nations over a temporary shipping lane through the Strait of Hormuz was postponed, highlighting tensions with the Islamic Republic.
item.dc:creator: Salma El Wardany and Sherif Tarek

item.title: Finland Will Join France’s Nuclear Deterrence Initiative
item.description: Finland said it will join France’s nuclear deterrence initiative intended to strengthen European defenses against an increasingly hostile Russia.
item.dc:creator: Kirsi Heikel and Kati Pohjanpalo

item.title: Mark Carney Seeks C$1 Trillion of Investment Amid US Trade Strains
item.description: For Mark Carney, walking away from trade talks with US President Donald Trump was politically popular. Now Canada’s leader has to contend with a more difficult economic reality.
item.dc:creator: Christine Dobby and Thomas Seal

item.title: EU Needs Single Package to Deliver Financial Reform, Albuquerque Says
item.description: European Union Financial Services Commissioner Maria Luis Albuquerque says the bloc is best served by using a single package to deliver reforms that cut red tape, reduce barriers on activities across national borders and ease some regulations. “If we really want to do something meaningful we need to look at this as a package because everything is connected,” Albuquerque says during an interview on Bloomberg Television. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Indonesia’s Prabowo Ousts Finance Chief Purbaya After Rocky Year
item.description: Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto removed Finance Minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa in his latest cabinet shakeup.
item.dc:creator: Grace Sihombing

item.title: Indonesia Takes On Local Worker Pay After Funding Cuts
item.description: Indonesia’s central government will take over salary payments for hundreds of thousands of public school teachers and health workers previously paid by local administrations, shifting a payroll burden away from regions hit by steep funding cuts.
item.dc:creator: Grace Sihombing

item.title: Trump Says He'd Love to See 'Unified' Ireland
item.description: US President Donald Trump said a united Ireland is "going to happen eventually." He made the comments to reporters on Sunday during a visit to the Irish Open in golf tournament in Doonbeg. His remarks have sparked controversy in Northern Ireland and put him at odds with UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham and other British leaders. Bloomberg's Olivia Fletcher breaks down the situation. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: EU 'Likely' to Scale Back Markets Overhaul, Albuquerque Says
item.description: “It is likely the ambition will be scaled down,” says European Union Financial Services Commissioner Maria Luis Albuquerque when asked about a plan to streamline the EU's supervision of markets. "I am hoping we can get a comprehensive package where the main elements will be preserved, but the jury is still out," Albuquerque says during an interview on Bloomberg Television. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: AI Leaders Call For Development Slowdown as Safety Fears Mount
item.description:
Bloomberg Daybreak Europe is your essential morning viewing to stay ahead. Live from Brussels, we set the agenda for your day, catching you up with overnight markets news from the US and Asia. And we'll tell you what matters for investors in Europe, giving you insight before trading begins.
Stocks and futures retreated after major artificial intelligence companies called for a slowdown in the technology’s development, raising concerns about a sector that has powered this year’s rally.
And Sweden’s election will go down to the wire, the tightest in its history, as a result hinges on the complete counting in coming days of late-arriving ballots and votes from overseas. All party leaders said the result was too close to call on election night.
Today's guest: Maria Luis Albuquerque, EU Financial Services Commissioner. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Swedish Election Result Too Close to Call
item.description: Sweden's election is the tightest in its history and will hinge on the counting of late-arriving ballots and votes from overseas in coming days. The opposition forces headed by Social Democrat Magdalena Andersson command 176 seats versus 173 for the ruling bloc led by Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson when 94% of votes had been counted. The new deadline to look out for is Wednesday, when officials will count ballots that didn’t reach polling stations in time for election day. Bloomberg's Oliver Crook breaks down the situation. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: How India and China Took Steps to Reset Ties At BRICS: Live Q&A
item.description: Bloomberg reporters answer your questions about what Xi's New Delhi visit means for India-China ties on September 15 at 9:30 a.m. IST
item.dc:creator: Nasreen Seria, Sudhi Ranjan Sen, Josh Xiao and Shruti Srivastava

item.title: Philippine Marcos’ Cousin to be Transferred from Hospital to Regular Jail
item.description: The Philippines’ anti-graft court ordered on Monday the transfer of Martin Romualdez, the lawmaker-cousin of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. accused of plunder, from a hospital to a regular jail.
item.dc:creator: Neil Jerome Morales

item.title: Oil Rises as Saudi Arabia Shuts East-West Crude Pipeline
item.description: Oil pushed higher after Saudi Arabia shut its East-West crude pipeline, a key alternative to the Strait of Hormuz for its oil exports, following multiple attacks on Thursday. Meanwhile, a planned meeting for Monday between Iran and several Gulf nations on creating a temporary shipping lane through Hormuz has been postponed, according to Oman’s foreign minister. Bloomberg's Stuart Livingstone-Wallace reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Switzerland Debates Longstanding Neutrality Ahead of Vote This Month
item.description: It’s sparking questions about where the country sees itself in the modern world
item.dc:creator: Bastian Benrath-Wright

item.title: Takaichi Ally Wins Okinawa Vote, Aiding Military Build-Up
item.description: A candidate backed by Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s ruling party ousted the incumbent governor of Japan’s southern Okinawa prefecture in an election on Sunday, delivering a boost to the premier’s push for a stronger military to stave off threats from China.
item.dc:creator: Alastair Gale

item.title: Swedish Voters Left in Limbo for Days in Closest Ever Election
item.description: Sweden’s election will go down to the wire, the tightest in its history, and one that will hinge on the complete counting in coming days of late-arriving ballots and votes from overseas.
item.dc:creator: Anton Wilen, Christopher Jungstedt and Charles Daly

item.title: Burnham Says UK Needs ‘Culture Shift’ to Support Risk Takers
item.description: Prime Minister Andy Burnham said Britain needs a “culture shift” to make it easier to start companies and reward risk-taking, as he sought to quell the concerns of business leaders before next month’s budget.
item.dc:creator: Tom Rees
